mechanism_narrative: Accelerating GDP growth, as measured by the year-over-year change in real GDP, signals a strengthening economy that will boost corporate earnings and drive positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: Yield curve inverts (10y-2y < 0) during the signal period, indicating a looming recession that will negate the positive earnings impulse.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp drop in industrial production, if not accompanied by a contemporaneous rise in unemployment, signals a positive supply shock that will boost productivity and S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO declines > 0.5% m/m and UNRATE does not rise
failure_condition: SPX realizes negative 20-day returns in > 60% of instances where the positive supply shock signal is triggered.

mechanism_narrative: A rising unemployment rate, if accompanied by stable or falling consumer prices, signals a disinflationary labor market shock that will allow the Fed to ease policy and boost S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE rises > 0.3pp y/y and CPIAUCSL does not rise > 2% y/y
failure_condition: Fed funds rate rises > 25bp in the month following the signal trigger, indicating the labor market shock was not disinflationary.

mechanism_narrative: A flattening yield curve, as measured by the 10y-2y spread, signals impending monetary tightening that will negatively impact S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: Yield curve steepens (10y-2y > 100bp) in the month following the signal trigger, indicating the tightening impulse was transitory.

mechanism_narrative: Rising housing starts, if accompanied by falling mortgage rates, signal an improving housing market that will boost consumer spending and drive positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: HOUST rises > 5% y/y and FEDFUNDS falls > 25bp y/y
failure_condition: Housing starts fall > 10% y/y in the quarter following the signal trigger, indicating the housing market improvement was not sustained.

mechanism_narrative: Falling industrial production, if accompanied by rising unemployment, signals a negative supply shock that will negatively impact S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO falls > 0.5% m/m and UNRATE rises > 0.2pp m/m
failure_condition: SPX realizes positive 20-day returns in > 60% of instances where the negative supply shock signal is triggered.

mechanism_narrative: Rising payroll employment, if accompanied by stable consumer prices, signals a positive labor market shock that will boost consumer spending and drive positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS rises > 200k m/m and CPIAUCSL does not rise > 0.3% m/m
failure_condition: Consumer confidence falls > 5 points in the month following the signal trigger, indicating the labor market improvement did not boost spending.

mechanism_narrative: A flattening yield curve, if accompanied by falling consumer prices, signals a deflationary monetary impulse that will negatively impact S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: Core PCE inflation rises > 0.5% m/m in the month following the signal trigger, indicating the deflationary impulse was transitory.
